rv.q: CST's production is astonishingly well executed and the perfect Pride month tribute to Ludlam's specific genius.

Central Square Theater’s fantastically entertaining production is helmed by David R. Gammons (previous CST directing credits include Vanity Fair and Frankenstein ) who directs Melendy and Graetz with the specificity and finesse of a world-class choreographer.
"The Mystery of Irma Vep" goes and stays so far over the top, with such conviction and abandon, that it comes out on the other side as something vividly real and even moving.

Cast members Gabriel Graetz and Paul Melendy exquisitely navigate the precise beats and improvisational moments needed to pull off the frenetic pace of the comedy, leaving the audience, and their characters, in stitches.
But, is the play fun, hilarious and entertaining? Yes, yes, and yes.

Ludlam's creation of a script that could keep an audience laughing and engaged nearly 40 years after his death suggests that he did, after all, emerge the victor in his own struggle against mortality.
Graetz and Melendy supply nearly all the fuel this production needs to take glorious flight.

Performing Arts , Theatre REVIEW: Comedic suspense and more drives Central Square Theater’s ‘The Mystery of Irma Vep: A Penny Dreadful’ Posted on June 15 by The Sleepless Critic Mummies and vampires and werewolves – oh my! However, as Paul Melendy as Nicodemus quips, “Don’t be skeered.”

Despite clever lines such as... Gammons's well-paced direction, the play was not really my cup of tea. It is lightweight, and campy, but a little too long and not quite pointed enough in the satire for my taste.
